places.name: Halle
places.country: Duchy of Magdeburg, Brandenburg-Prussia (today Germany)
places.what: Born to a barber-surgeon; the church organist Zachow was his only teacher.

places.name: Halle Domkirche
places.country: Duchy of Magdeburg, Brandenburg-Prussia (today Germany)
places.what: Matriculated at the university, then took the post of organist at the Calvinist cathedral on probation.

places.name: Oper am Gänsemarkt, Hamburg
places.country: Free Imperial City of Hamburg (today Germany)
places.what: Violinist, later harpsichordist, in the opera orchestra; a quarrel with Mattheson in 1704 nearly killed him.

places.name: Oper am Gänsemarkt, Hamburg
places.country: Free Imperial City of Hamburg (today Germany)
places.what: His first opera, composed at nineteen; Nero followed the same year.

places.name: Florence
places.country: Grand Duchy of Tuscany (today Italy)
places.what: Went to Italy at the Medici invitation; his first all-Italian opera, Rodrigo, was staged at the Cocomero theatre.

places.name: Rome
places.country: Papal States (today Italy)
places.what: Opera was banned, so he wrote sacred music for the clergy, including Dixit Dominus, for Ruspoli and Ottoboni.

places.name: Ruspoli palace, Rome
places.country: Papal States (today Italy)
places.what: Staged on Easter Sunday in the palace’s ground-floor hall for the patron Marchese Ruspoli.

places.name: Naples
places.country: Kingdom of Naples (Habsburg rule; today Italy)
places.what: The serenata for Duchess Aurora Sanseverino’s circle; the score is dated 16 June 1708.

places.name: Teatro San Giovanni Grisostomo, Venice
places.country: Republic of Venice (today Italy)
places.what: Premiered at the Grimani family theatre; an unprecedented run of 27 consecutive performances followed.

places.name: Hanover
places.country: Electorate of Hanover (today Germany)
places.what: Kapellmeister to the Elector George, the future George I; he left at the end of the year.

places.name: Queen’s Theatre, Haymarket, London
places.country: Kingdom of Great Britain (today United Kingdom)
places.what: His first London opera, written for the Queen’s Theatre in the Haymarket.

places.name: Barn Elms, Surrey
places.country: Kingdom of Great Britain (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Lived at Mathew Andrews’s estate in summer, the year of the Utrecht Te Deum and Jubilate.

places.name: Cannons, Middlesex
places.country: Kingdom of Great Britain (today United Kingdom)
places.what: House composer to the Duke of Chandos; wrote the Chandos Anthems and Acis and Galatea.

places.name: River Thames, from Whitehall
places.country: Kingdom of Great Britain (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Performed from barges for George I, who boarded at Whitehall Palace about 8 p.m. on a Wednesday.

places.name: King’s Theatre, Haymarket, London
places.country: Kingdom of Great Britain (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Ran the Royal Academy of Music’s Italian operas; joint manager from 1729; over twenty-five of his operas premiered here.

places.name: 25 Brook Street, Mayfair, London
places.country: Kingdom of Great Britain (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Rented the newly built house for the rest of his life; Messiah was composed in London in 1741.

places.name: Sheldonian Theatre, Oxford
places.country: Kingdom of Great Britain (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Premiered for the Publick Act; Oxford offered an honorary doctorate, which he declined.

places.name: Covent Garden Theatre, London
places.country: Kingdom of Great Britain (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Opera seasons from 1734, then oratorios: Messiah in London (1743), Solomon (1749), and his last Messiah hearing.

places.name: Dublin
places.country: Kingdom of Ireland (today Republic of Ireland)
places.what: Invited by the Duke of Devonshire for hospital charity concerts; arranged a six-concert subscription series.

places.name: Great Music Hall, Fishamble Street, Dublin
places.country: Kingdom of Ireland (today Republic of Ireland)
places.what: Seven hundred people attended; men were asked to remove their swords and women to wear no hoops.

places.name: Green Park, London
places.country: Kingdom of Great Britain (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Played in a Servandoni-designed building; a public rehearsal at Vauxhall Gardens drew over twelve thousand.

places.name: Foundling Hospital, London
places.country: Kingdom of Great Britain (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Arranged a Messiah performance for the children’s home; annual charity performances followed until his death.

places.name: 25 Brook Street, London
places.country: Kingdom of Great Britain (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Died at home, aged 74, after attending Messiah at Covent Garden eight days earlier.

places.country: Kingdom of Great Britain (today United Kingdom)
